title: Algebra II — Advanced Patterns in God's Design
description: Test your understanding of polynomials, rational expressions, radicals, exponential and logarithmic functions, and sequences and series.

questions.question: What does the Fundamental Theorem of Algebra guarantee about a polynomial of degree n?
options: It has exactly n real zeros
It has exactly n zeros (counting multiplicity and complex zeros)
It has at most n/2 zeros
It has no zeros if n is odd
questions.explanation: The Fundamental Theorem of Algebra, proved by Gauss, states that every polynomial of degree n has exactly n zeros when counting multiplicity and including complex zeros. This guarantees that polynomial equations always have solutions.

questions.question: What is the factored form of x³ - 8?
questions.explanation: x³ - 8 is a difference of cubes: a³ - b³ = (a - b)(a² + ab + b²). With a = x and b = 2: x³ - 8 = (x - 2)(x² + 2x + 4).

questions.question: When solving a rational equation, why must you always check for extraneous solutions?
options: Because the equation might have no solutions at all
Because multiplying by the LCD can introduce solutions that make the original denominators zero
Because rational equations always have infinite solutions
questions.explanation: When you multiply both sides by the LCD to clear fractions, you may introduce solutions that make the original denominators equal to zero. These extraneous solutions must be identified and rejected because division by zero is undefined.

questions.question: What is the value of log₂(64)?
questions.explanation: log₂(64) asks: '2 raised to what power equals 64?' Since 2⁶ = 64, log₂(64) = 6.

questions.question: Which property of logarithms states that logb(MN) = logb(M) + logb(N)?
questions.explanation: The Product Rule for logarithms states that the logarithm of a product equals the sum of the logarithms. This property derives from the exponent rule bᵐ · bⁿ = bᵐ⁺ⁿ.

questions.question: A bacterial population doubles every 3 hours, starting with 200 bacteria. Which function models the population P after t hours?
questions.explanation: Since the population doubles (multiplied by 2) every 3 hours, the model is P(t) = 200 · 2^(t/3). When t = 3, P = 200 · 2¹ = 400 (doubled). When t = 6, P = 200 · 2² = 800 (doubled again).

questions.question: What is the sum of the infinite geometric series 8 + 4 + 2 + 1 + 1/2 + ...?
questions.explanation: This is a geometric series with a₁ = 8 and r = 1/2. Since |r| < 1, it converges. S = a₁/(1 - r) = 8/(1 - 1/2) = 8/(1/2) = 16.

questions.question: The Fibonacci sequence appears in sunflower spirals, pine cones, and flower petals. What does this suggest about the natural world?
options: These are random coincidences with no deeper meaning
Plants evolved to count Fibonacci numbers
A single mathematical pattern appearing across diverse organisms points to a common intelligent Designer
The Fibonacci sequence only appears in mathematics textbooks, not in nature
questions.explanation: The Fibonacci sequence and the Golden Ratio appear independently across many different species and structures in nature. The consistent appearance of one mathematical pattern in such diverse contexts points to a common Designer who embedded this mathematical beauty into creation.

questions.question: Solve: 3^(x+1) = 81
questions.explanation: Since 81 = 3⁴, the equation becomes 3^(x+1) = 3⁴. Setting exponents equal: x + 1 = 4, so x = 3.
